query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Systematic variation of elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr-HEA samples will reveal a cause-and-effect relationship between individual constituent percentages and mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Base composition of HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy (HEA) with unexplored individual constituent effects
generation.intervention: Controlled variation of elemental percentages (Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr) in HfNbTaTiZr-HEA samples
generation.conditions: Mechanical properties testing conditions, including tensile testing at a strain rate of 0.001 s^-1, hardness measurements using a Vickers indenter, and microstructural analysis using scanning electron microscopy
generation.structural_mediator: Grain size and phase composition, where the grain size affects the yield strength through the Hall-Petch relationship, and the phase composition influences the ductility through the formation of secondary phases
generation.mechanism: Changes in elemental percentages alter the grain size and phase composition, leading to variations in mechanical properties, as the addition of Hf increases the grain boundary energy, leading to a decrease in grain size, while the formation of secondary phases is influenced by the Nb and Ta contents
generation.predicted_outcome: A 10% increase in Hf content will result in a 15% increase in yield strength (from 800 MPa to 920 MPa) and a 5% decrease in ductility (from 20% to 19%) relative to the base composition, based on density functional theory calculations
generation.baseline: Base composition of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA with yield strength of 800 MPa and ductility of 20%
generation.boundary: Elemental percentages varied between 10% and 20% of the base composition for Hf, 15% and 25% for Nb, 10% and 20% for Ta, 15% and 25% for Ti, and 10% and 20% for Zr
generation.uncertainty: There may be interactions between the elements that affect the mechanical properties, and the predictions are based on simplified models that do not account for all possible effects

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with systematic variation of elemental percentages and measurement of mechanical properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength does not increase by at least 10% with a 10% increase in Hf content compared to the control sample with unchanged composition, the hypothesis is falsified
